synoptic.summary: A shortwave ridge moves east of Utah tonight, leaving a strengthening flow aloft from 180°–200° ahead of the next Pacific storm. Monday stays dry, but the southerly gradient (20–27 kt a few thousand feet up) keeps all three launches in flow from 140°–160° and suppresses the usual afternoon switch to 320°–360°. The storm arrives Tuesday: 26–38 kt aloft in the morning, rain 95% from 11:00 and a cold front crossing in the afternoon/evening, turning the flow westerly. Wednesday morning brings a light gradient (winds aloft under 15 kt) and the normal drainage before the next storm on Thursday. Thunder chances stay low (up to 8%).
synoptic.afd_excerpt: This will put Utah under an increasing southwesterly flow aloft through tomorrow ahead of the next storm system.

pressure.significance: Sea-level pressure at Salt Lake airport peaked at 1022.3 mb at 10:54 Sunday and fell to 1019.6 mb by 16:54 — the ridge is moving off and a trough is approaching, with Tuesday's cold front next.

observations.summary: Sunday-evening observations (15:55–17:05 local), all under 2 h old at fetch time: the south-valley stations show flow from 156°–180° at 3–11 kt (Spanish Fork 176°/8 kt G10, South Valley Regional 180°/8 kt, Alpine 168°/6 kt G8, Lehi 168°/3 kt G7), matching the southerly forecast. Salt Lake and Provo airports turned briefly to 240°–300° at 3–4 kt, then went calm. The Point of the Mountain and Draper stations returned no data. These are evening readings — they say little about Monday morning beyond confirming the southerly flow.
